title: A linked queue: front and back
summary: Add at the back, remove from the front. Two pointers keep both O(1).

checkpoints.text: The queue was empty, so the first node is both the front and the back.
20 joins at the back. The old back node (10) points at it, then `back` moves.
Dequeue takes from the front: 10 joined first, so it leaves first.
The last node just left. `front` became NULL by itself, but `back` still held the address of the deleted node. This line resets it; without it, the next enqueue would write into freed memory.
Because `back` was reset, 30 starts a fresh queue as both front and back.
First in, first out: 10, then 20, then 30 left in the order they joined.
